From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 8 Feb 2027 08:30:00 -0800
Subject: Internal: Benchmark sweep results (initial) — attached csv

Team,

Completed the qps sweep against the pilot prompt set (baseline model: rdx-13b-std): summary below, full output in benchmark_results_q1.csv.

Summary (median across prompt families):
- 10 TPS: p95=122ms, throughput=10 TPS sustained
- 30 TPS: p95=210ms, throughput=30 TPS sustained
- 60 TPS: p95=385ms, throughput=58 TPS sustained (some tail spikes)
- 90 TPS: p95=610ms, throughput=75 TPS sustained (falling off due to KV eviction)

Observations:
- KV cache warmup critical: cold-start p95 at 60TPS ~540ms, warm window improves ~35%.
- At sustained 60-90 TPS memory pressure causes periodic stalls; reconfiguring chunk size and increasing local KV capacity buys stability.
- Quantized variant rdx-13b-q4_1 drops p95 by ~25% but introduces minor regression on long-form summarization quality (subjective).

Actionable next steps (owners):
- Karthik: run targeted warmup scenarios + longer runs (30m) to validate steady-state (due Feb 12).
- Diego: test KV capacity bump (mem + config) and optimized chunking (due Feb 14).
- Marissa: confirm customer acceptance criteria around occasional quality delta vs cost (due Feb 12).

Attachments: benchmark_results_q1.csv (120KB)

- Diego
Senior Inference Engineer, Redwood Inference

Date: Wed, 10 Feb 2027 16:47:00 -0800
Subject: MAP checkpoint (Feb 10) — perf playback + agreed next steps

Sanjay / Amal —

Thanks for joining today[0m[0m[0m[0m[0m for the checkpoint. Below is a concise playback of the performance work and our recommended tuning path.

What we ran: qps sweep across representative prompt families. Full CSV attached for your team to inspect.

Key results (customer-facing):
- Baseline rdx-13b-std meets p95 <350ms up to ~40 TPS; above 40 TPS we see tail increases driven by KV churn and cold-starts.
- Quantized variant (rdx-13b-q4_1) reduces p95 by ~25% at 60TPS but shows occasional quality diffs on long summaries.

Recommended next steps (timeline & owners):
- Warmup policy (Diego) — implement a short prefix warmup for session-based flows; target rollout Feb 14.
- KV tuning (Diego) — increase local KV allocation + adjust chunking; validate by Feb 14.
- Extended steady-state runs (Karthik) — 30m runs at 60/90 TPS to confirm stability; due Feb 12.
- Customer quality signoff (Marissa / OptiMed) — Marissa to collect OptiMed feedback on q4_1 quality delta; signoff due Feb 16.
- Final close call (Dylan / OptiMed) — propose Feb 17 10am PT for decision and next contract steps.

Links / artifacts: HubSpot deal RD-2027-OPT-09, MAP spreadsheet, bench CSV (attached).

If OptiMed prefers a lower-cost path vs strict quality, we can propose an autoscale policy that routes non-critical traffic to q4_1 and critical flows to rdx-13b-std. Happy to walk through tradeoffs on the call Feb 17.

Regards,
Dylan Brooks
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
